events.summary: Economists Erik Brynjolfsson, Bharat Chandar, and Danielle Chen released a paper titled "Canaries in the Coal Mine? They report substantial declines in employment for early-career workers aged 22–25 in AI-exposed occupations such as software development and customer service, while employment for experienced workers in the same occupations remained stable or grew. events.title: Economic Innovation Group researchers publish findings on AI employment effects
events.summary: Sarah Eckhardt and Nathan Goldschlag of the Economic Innovation Group released research examining the relationship between AI exposure and recent employment trends. Using five different measures of job exposure to AI, they found no detectable difference in unemployment between workers in more-exposed versus less-exposed occupations for three of the five measures, including their preferred measure from Felten (2021). For two measures, they identified only a small difference of 0.2 to 0.3 percentage points. The researchers concluded that AI probably is not yet destroying jobs, or if it is, the effect remains very small.

events.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics released August employment data showing only 22,000 jobs added to the U.S. economy, with unemployment at 4.3% and the broader jobless rate jumping to 8.1%. events.title: Trump issues executive order modifying reciprocal tariffs and establishing trade agreement procedures
events.summary: President Trump issued an executive order on September 5, 2025, modifying the scope of reciprocal tariffs imposed under prior orders and establishing procedures for implementing trade and security framework agreements with foreign partners. The order delegates authority to the Secretary of Commerce and U.S. Trade Representative to implement framework and final trade agreements, permits tariff modifications to zero percent for aligned trading partners on specified product categories, and updates the list of goods exempt from reciprocal duties. The order invokes the International Emergency Economic Powers Act and Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act as authority.
events.why_relevant: The order expands executive authority over trade policy by establishing unilateral procedures for tariff modification tied to bilateral negotiations, potentially circumventing congressional trade authority and affecting domestic prices, supply chains, and international economic relations.
